For anyone who needs this now, I've published an OpenCode plugin that addresses this issue as a temporary workaround while a native fix is developed:

**[`@gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity)** — source at https://github.com/gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity

It uses the `experimental.chat.system.transform` hook (seeded by `experimental.chat.messages.transform`) to inject a one-liner into the system prompt each turn:

> You are currently operating as the "build" agent.

### Installation

Add to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["@gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity"]
}
```

I've been running it through a full QA cycle (switching plan → build → plan → build) and it correctly updates the identity on each agent transition.

Happy to answer questions if anyone tries it out.

I ended up publishing a plugin that addresses this as a workaround while native support is developed:

**[`@gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity)** — source at https://github.com/gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity

It uses the `experimental.chat.messages.transform` hook to prepend a `[agent: X]` header to each assistant message's first text part before it reaches the LLM — so every agent (including Retrospective) sees attributed messages like:

```
[agent: plan]
Here is the analysis you requested...
```

The mutation is ephemeral — it only affects what the model sees per call, without altering the persisted database.

### Installation

Add to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["@gotgenes/opencode-agent-identity"]
}
```

The package also includes `AgentSelfIdentityPlugin` (for #7492), so you get both behaviors in one install.

I've verified this works with my Retrospective agent — it can now reliably attribute each turn to the correct agent.

Confirming the same issue. After installing the CLI through the Desktop menu, I also encountered `zsh: killed opencode`.

Upon inspection, it was found that `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` lacks a code signature:  
Running `codesign -v ~/.opencode/bin/opencode` shows that it is unsigned.

Temporary solution:  
Run `sudo codesign --force --deep --sign - ~/.opencode/bin/opencode`.

Suggestion: The OpenCode release process should ensure that all distribution channels (installation scripts, Desktop, npm, and auto-updates) provide binaries with proper code signing.

Please implement background compaction as in Copilot CLI: start compaction in background at 80% context utilization (`COPILOT_BACKGROUND_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD`), while the agent continues working normally (sending requests, calling tools). When compaction completes, the summary replaces old messages but messages generated during compaction are preserved — so the agent retains recent context and doesn't lose direction. At 95% utilization (`COPILOT_BUFFER_EXHAUSTION_THRESHOLD`), block until compaction finishes. I love how Copilot implements this.
